description: [This Day] Airtel Africa has reiterated its commitment to delivering unmatched experience to its 183.5 million customers through continuous investment in its network, advanced technologies and strategic partnerships to further expand its coverage and capacity to drive digital and financial inclusion on the continent.
title: Africa: Airtel Africa Reaffirms Commitment to Customer Service Delivery

description: [New Dawn] MONROVIA, October 12, 2026 -- Morocco is preparing to propose a new migration cooperation strategy to its international partners, following concerns raised by King Mohammed VI that existing arrangements are no longer adequate to address recurring migration challenges.
title: Africa: Morocco Plans New Migration Cooperation Strategy

description: [RootsToFoods Capital Series] In a RootsToFoods Capital Series interview, Wasim Tahir, Senior Advisor at ODI Global and former director at British International Investment, explains how development finance actually moves private capital into emerging markets, and why the lasting answer lies in deep domestic capital markets and national development banks.
title: Africa: To Finance Africa at Scale, Build Its Capital Markets at Home

description: [New Times] Frenchman Alain Prost claimed the last of his four Formula One world championships at the Kyalami Circuit near Johannesburg, South Africa, in 1993, the last time the continent hosted a Grand Prix. The event's subsequent collapse brought Formula One's presence in Africa to an abrupt end.
title: Africa: Rwanda Set to Welcome Formula One Back to Africa, 30 Years Later

description: [Independent (Kampala)] Africa's gaming industry is shifting from a story about how many people play games to one about how much of the industry can be built around those players.
title: Africa: Africa's 406 Million Gamers Are Triggering a Race to Build the Business Around Them

description: [ISS] Anthropic's threat report reveals how AI is making cyberattacks and influence campaigns faster, more scalable and harder to detect.
title: Africa: Africa Must Prepare for AI-Powered Cyber Threats At Scale

description: [The Conversation Africa] The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences has awarded this year's Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences to the American economists Robert E. Hall and Michael Woodford. The prize was awarded in recognition of their development of macroeconomic models that helped to reduce the length and depth of economic downturns.
title: Africa: Economics Nobel - How This Year's Winners Helped to Smooth the Cycle of Economic Peaks and Troughs

description: [Vanguard] Former President of the African Development Bank (AfDB), Dr Akinwumi Adesina, has urged African leaders to prioritise investment in education, healthcare, skills development, technology and entrepreneurship to unlock the economic potential of the continent's growing youth population.
title: Africa: Adesina Urges Investment in Youths to Unlock Africa's Potential

description: [Capital FM] Nairobi -- The United Nations General Assembly has adopted a political declaration calling for stronger global cooperation to prevent and respond to future pandemics, with the United States, Israel and Argentina voting against the text.
title: Africa: UN Adopts Pandemic Declaration As U.S., Israel and Argentina Vote Against

description: [allAfrica]
title: Africa: All of Africa Today - October 13, 2026

description: [The Independent Panel] A Statement from the Friends of the High-Level Meeting on Pandemic Prevention, Preparedness and Response
title: Africa: We Applaud the Adoption of The Political Declaration But Say: Now Countries Must Make Good On Their Words

description: [WHO] The Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC), of which WHO is a member, today issued a Food Insecurity and Malnutrition Alert for Sudan.
title: Africa: IPC Sudan Food Insecurity and Malnutrition Alert

description: [Nigeria Health Watch] The World Health Organization (WHO) launched a new five-year strategy for its Hub for Pandemic and Epidemic Intelligence, charting a path towards a world where every country can detect and understand emerging health threats within 24 hours of their appearance by 2030. Strengthening rapid detection is a cornerstone of global health security, helping countries contain outbreaks before they escalate into larger epidemics or spread internationally.
title: Africa: WHO Pandemic Hub Sets Ambitious Goal to Detect New Outbreaks Within 24 Hours

description: [Ghanaian Times] Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa has assured Ghanaians that the government remains ready to evacuate nationals from South Africa if their lives are threatened by further attacks.
title: Africa: Ghana Will Resume Evacuations From South Africa If Lives Are Threatened - Ablakwa

description: [Daily News] Dar es Salaam -- THE Deputy Minister for Foreign Affairs and East African Cooperation, James Millya, has called for professional, impartial and evidence-based election observation to strengthen democracy, peace and stability across Africa.
title: Africa: Tanzania Calls for Credible Election Observation to Advance Africa's Peace, Stability

description: [UN News] The General Assembly on Monday adopted a political declaration on pandemic prevention, preparedness and response, by 153 in favour to three against (Argentina, Israel and United States) with two abstentions (New Zealand and Paraguay).
title: Africa: General Assembly Adopts Pandemic Declaration, but Not By Consensus

description: [The Conversation Africa] Most children who are infected with SARS-COV2, the virus that causes COVID, experience only mild symptoms or no symptoms at all. But a small proportion develop severe illness which can sometimes even require hospital care.
title: Africa: Why Do Some Children Become Seriously Ill With Covid? the Answer May Lie in Their Genes

description: [The Conversation Africa] Not every snakebite injects venom. When venom enters the body, however, it can cause snake envenoming. This is a potentially fatal condition and it mostly affects poor rural communities across tropical and subtropical regions who don't have easy access to medical care.
title: Africa: Snakebites Are a Far Bigger Problem Than We Knew - New Study Maps the Hidden Dangers

description: [UN News] The money is running out faster than needs are growing: with 117 million men, women and children now forced from their homes, the UN refugee agency (UNHCR) has received just $3 billion of the $8.5 billion it needs this year - and its chief, Barham Salih, warns that the global support system for asylum-seekers risks buckling.
title: Africa: 'Efficiency Has Limits' - UNHCR Chief Warns Refugee Protection Is Buckling Under Cuts

description: [CJID] The Centre for Journalism Innovation and Development (CJID) will launch SautiHealth, a technology-enabled platform for monitoring, analysing, and summarising public statements by health sector professionals, leaders, and institutions across Africa. The platform is an initiative of the CJID developed in partnership with the US-based research nonprofit Media Ecosystem Analysis Group (MEAG) to strengthen access to structured and verifiable public health information across the continent.
title: Africa: CJID, MEAG to Launch Health Discourse Monitoring Platform
